items: Audit Your Scope and Evidence: Create a three-column scope audit worksheet listing every contracted item, its completion status, and supporting evidence to establish objective facts about what was agreed versus what actually exists.

Audit Your Scope and Evidence: Photograph and video every defective area with visible timestamps, documenting the exact date you first noticed each problem so your evidence holds up legally if disputes arise.

Audit Your Scope and Evidence: Separate all change orders into a tracking document noting whether each modification was signed by both parties or agreed to verbally, since unsigned changes are nearly unenforceable.

Audit Your Scope and Evidence: Conduct a physical walkthrough of the property with your scope audit worksheet in hand, recording video of the actual state of all work to create a timestamped visual record for your case.

Deploy Legal Protections Now: File a preliminary lien notice against your property within your state's required timeframe to protect your right to claim against the property itself for any amounts still owed or work not completed.

Deploy Legal Protections Now: Consult a construction attorney immediately since stop-payment rights, preliminary lien deadlines, and back charge procedures all have strict statutory timeframes that vary by state and expire quickly.

Deploy Legal Protections Now: Send all future communications to your contractor exclusively in writing through email or certified mail to create a verifiable paper trail that can be used as evidence in any dispute.

Deploy Legal Protections Now: Issue a formal written scope freeze to your contractor stating that no additional work will be authorized or paid for until existing defects are resolved and both parties agree on a remediation plan.

Secure Your Financial Position: Send a stop-payment instruction to your bank or escrow agent for any scheduled contractor payments until you fully understand your legal position and can make informed financial decisions.

Secure Your Financial Position: Create a complete accounting of every payment made with dates, amounts, and purposes, then add up all additional costs you've incurred from delays, defective work, or hiring replacement contractors.

Secure Your Financial Position: Review your contract for any liquidated damages clauses, delay penalties, or completion guarantees that work in your favor and can be used as leverage in negotiations or claims.

Secure Your Financial Position: Send a certified letter to your contractor formally documenting all defects, incomplete work, and missed deadlines while demanding resolution within a reasonable timeframe to establish the breach on record.
